## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Kilesasaṁkilesikaduka* (Patthana 8.53) is a canonical Abhidhamma text belonging to the Paṭṭhāna section of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Like other sections of the Paṭṭhāna, it investigates causal conditioning and reciprocal conditional relations (paccaya) applied through the analytical dyad (duka) of phenomena that are defilements and corruptible states (*kilesa-saṁkilesika*) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are listed by SuttaCentral or detected with significant similarity by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis shows extensive internal reuse within the Pali Abhidhamma, sharing 111 textual passages with 30 other texts, predominantly across other books and sections of the Paṭṭhāna [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual alignments occur with other treatments of the defilement cluster (*kilesagocchaka*), notably *Kilesagocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.12, sharing 4,105 characters), *Kilesagocchaka* (Patthana 2.12), and adjacent defilement dyads in chapter 8, such as *Kilesasaṁkiliṭṭhaduka* (Patthana 8.54), *Kilesakilesasampayuttaduka* (Patthana 8.55), *Kilesavippayuttasaṁkilesikaduka* (Patthana 8.56), and *Kilesasampayuttaduka* (Patthana 8.52) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits standard conditioning formulas shared with root-condition dyads such as *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1) and *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
